say: In 1925 Victor Lustig, posing as a deputy director-general of the Ministry of Posts and Telegraphs, used fake government letterheads and invited scrap metal dealers to a confidential meeting at an expensive hotel, saying the tower would be sold for scrap and must stay secret to avoid public outcry.
check: manual: names and story only, no numbers

say: Andre Poisson paid for the tower plus a large bribe; Lustig fled to Austria with the money; Poisson was too embarrassed to go to the police; Lustig returned later that year, tried again, police were informed, he fled to the US.
check: manual: sources disagree on amounts and the delay before the second attempt (one month vs six months), so the script names neither

say: The Eiffel Tower was built as the centrepiece of the 1889 World's Fair.
Maintenance needs 60 tons of paint every 7 years to prevent rust.
The wrought iron structure weighs 7,300 tons (tonnes).
